headline: Fined $811m, immigrant bail firms' scams reportedly went on
pages: A BBC investigation says operations tied to Libre by Nexus, once the largest immigration bail company in the US, kept charging detained migrants after its founders were fined $811m in 2024 for defrauding clients. One detainee, Mildred Juarez, said friends wired $2,600 to Libre Immigration Services, recommended by her lawyer, yet she stayed in a Texas detention center for a month while being told her bond was unpaid. The BBC says that company was owned by a convicted fraudster who had acquired assets of the earlier firm, which had appeared to shut down. Public records and interviews with clients and former employees point to a tangle of linked businesses and a continuing flow of cash.

Demand for bond companies has grown as ICE has made more than 1.2m arrests since President Trump returned to office. Conditions in detention centers can be poor, advocates and government reports say. Source: BBC.
